NATO = a military alliance of North American and European countries
humanitarian aid = food, medicine and shelter given to people in a crisis
sanctions = penalties, often economic, imposed on a country to change its behaviour
asylum seeker = a person who has applied for protection in another country and is waiting for a decision
refugee = a person who has fled their country because of war or persecution and been granted protection
member state = a country that belongs to an international organisation such as the EU
diplomatic relations = official political relations between countries
consular assistance = official help a country gives its citizens abroad
ambassador = the senior diplomat who represents a country abroad
peacekeeping = international military or civilian operations that help keep a ceasefire
ceasefire = an agreement to stop fighting for a period of time
economic migrant = a person who moves to another country mainly to work and improve their living standard
displaced person = someone forced to leave their home, often still inside their own country
deportation = forcing a person to leave a country by official order
development aid = money and expertise given to poorer countries to support long-term progress
developing country = a country with a lower average income and less industrialised economy
international law = rules that states have agreed should govern relations between them
freedom of religion = the right to hold, change or practise a faith, or to have none
place of worship = a building or site used for religious practice, such as a church, mosque or synagogue
separation of church and state = the principle that religious institutions should not run the government, and vice versa
